name: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park
description: On the Big Island of Hawaiʻi, this park protects two of the planet's most active volcanoes: Kīlauea and Mauna Loa, the world's largest shield volcano, which rises 4,170 metres. Eruptions keep reshaping the terrain, leaving fresh lava fields, steaming craters and glowing Halemaʻumaʻu. Between the lava, you can walk through forests of giant ferns and spot rare native birds.
